title: Whiplash — a Cinematic Story Edit
description: Build tension with dialogue, bold captions and an accelerating finish. Adapt the workflow to your own footage.
promptSource: Adaptable prompt derived from the saved Whiplash edit’s source inspection, timeline, caption layouts and production records. The shown video was made in an earlier reference-reconstruction run, not generated by this new prompt. Film: Whiplash (2014). Music: Grant Steller, Every Living Breathing Moment. Source footage and music are not part of the open-source toolkit.
prompt:
Use Video Use to turn my supplied or licensed footage into a cinematic story edit. Carry forward the subject, audience, format, length and level of involvement already established in this conversation. If no length is set, aim for 45–60 seconds. Adapt the editing language of this example to my material; choose new shots and words that fit my story.

Inspect the footage and transcribe the useful dialogue before choosing cuts. Find a clear subject, a goal, an obstacle and a payoff. Use only events and spoken words supported by the source. Open with a compelling line or visible action, hold long enough to understand the stakes, then alternate effort, resistance and reactions. Give the strongest setback a little breathing room. Build toward a final 6–10 seconds of shorter, energetic shots that show the payoff. Keep that final burst mostly free of text. Preserve the meaning of dialogue and the order of any process being demonstrated.

Use mostly clean hard cuts. Let expressions, eyelines and movement motivate each cut; save the fastest cutting for the finish. Keep natural motion unless a deliberate speed change improves a specific moment. Use a restrained, high-contrast grade with believable skin tones and consistent shots within each setting.

Add selective, bold, uppercase slab-serif captions in white, with a few important words in red. Build short phrases in sync with actual speech, placing them in available negative space. Leave uncaptained passages for the images to breathe. Keep text readable and clear of faces, hands and important action throughout the cue. If the footage supports it, use one brief isolated-subject-on-black moment at the emotional peak, then return to the scene. Omit it if a clean moving matte cannot be achieved.

Edit dialogue and music on separate timelines. Choose a licensed or original track whose changing intensity supports the story. Align key transitions to its actual phrases and accents rather than forcing every cut onto a fixed beat grid. Keep dialogue clear, music continuous across picture cuts, and sound effects sparse and motivated. Avoid clipped words, cut clicks and an abruptly truncated music tail.

Render the agreed format with current Video Use tools and retain an editable EDL, caption timing, fonts, audio decisions and source credits. Check the encoded cut boundaries, speech alignment, moving text/subject collisions, first frame and final hold; decode the complete file and verify both audio and picture duration. Follow the existing involvement mode, including a short approval snippet before the full edit in hands-on mode.

title: Dead Air Removal
description: Remove pauses and repeated speech from a camera unboxing.
prompt: Tighten this unboxing footage into a natural 12–15 second clip. Find one useful complete thought about the camera, then remove hesitations, repeated words, long pauses, and time spent fumbling with packaging. Keep the speaker’s real voice and meaning. Use clean cuts and only a small change in crop when it helps cover a jump. Keep the product visible. No music, flashy transitions, title cards, or decorative overlays.

title: Detail Crop
description: Select clear product views from a long unboxing.
prompt: Turn this raw camera unboxing into a clear 12–15 second product showcase. Skip the packaging struggle and find three genuinely useful views of the camera: the full product, a close detail being handled, and a satisfying finished view. Cut when the hands move naturally and use careful close crops to show what matters. Hold each detail long enough to understand it. Keep real handling sounds; omit incomplete speech. No invented features, music, graphic frames, or unnecessary text.

title: Process Cutdown
description: Condense packaging and setup into a short reveal.
prompt: Turn the slow box-opening and setup in this unboxing footage into a satisfying 12–15 second reveal. Show a brief sealed-box or wrapped-product moment, keep only the decisive opening and assembly actions, and finish on the camera fully revealed and ready to use. Remove searching, repeated handling, empty hands, and long gaps. Preserve the real order of events and keep clean original handling sounds. No added music, fake product facts, title cards, or flashy transitions.

title: Vertical Reframe
description: Reframe a product demonstration for a vertical short.
prompt: Make a useful 12–15 second vertical short from this widescreen camera-unboxing footage. Choose one complete product demonstration with an actual reveal or useful takeaway. Cut the idle handling and pauses, reframe each shot to keep the camera and the demonstrator’s hands visible, and move the crop only when the product moves. Keep any included speech intact and add clean accurate phrase captions within safe margins. Use the speaker’s own voice and real sounds. No blurred background bars, stretching, fake words, music, or decorative transitions.

title: Speed Ramp
description: Acceleration, a slow-motion peak, and cuts that follow the action.
prompt: Use only the supplied Tears of Steel source video to make a 12-second widescreen action edit called Velocity. Inspect the source first and choose four genuinely energetic shots with clear camera or subject motion; avoid dialogue-only holds and credits. Build a readable arc: 0–2s an intriguing moving detail, 2–5s three escalating action cuts, 5–8s one hero movement that eases from 100% to 45% speed for its peak then accelerates to 220%, 8–11s a decisive payoff, 11–12s a clean visual finish. Cut on matching movement directions and use two 6-frame whip transitions only where source motion supports them. Add a single 6% punch-in on the strongest impact. Preserve sharp faces and edges; use frame sampling if interpolation bends objects. Keep original environmental sound where useful, add a restrained original percussive pulse and two synchronized impacts, and duck the pulse under any retained intelligible speech. No stock footage, no new generated scenes, no full-screen captions, and no random flash/glitch effects. Deliver one polished 1920x1080 H264 MP4 with intentional crops, no stretched image, plus source timecodes and an edit decision list. The edit must still clearly communicate acceleration and payoff when muted.

title: Freeze Frame Poster
description: A moving shot becomes an editorial poster, then returns to motion.
prompt: Turn the same supplied Tears of Steel source into a 12-second widescreen moving film poster. Choose one continuous shot with at least 6 seconds of usable motion with a clear expressive character or striking mechanical silhouette. Start full-screen in motion for 2.5s; stop precisely on the strongest pose with a clean 8-frame camera ease, then animate the frozen image into a large offset rectangular crop over a warm ivory background. Reveal three small close-up tiles from that exact same frame—an eye or face detail, a mechanical detail, and a texture—with precise staggered slides. Use bold condensed black typography reading 'A MOMENT / IN MOTION', one small burnt-orange index '01', and thin alignment rules. Keep the frozen hero recognizably photographic and let scale/position supply depth; do not attempt a rough automatic cutout. Hold the completed editorial poster from 6.5–9s, then resolve the tiles into the full original frame and resume its source motion from the exact held frame for the final 3s. Use restrained dry camera clicks and the source ambience. No footage beyond the one source. Deliver 1920x1080 H264 MP4, crisp type, generous margins, no unreadable microtext, source timecodes, and the edit decision list.

title: Animated Split Screen
description: Three views share the frame and exchange emphasis.
prompt: Create a 12-second 1920x1080 widescreen editorial split-screen film using only the same supplied Tears of Steel source. Pick one short sequence with a clear subject and useful wide, medium, and close-up views. Open as one uninterrupted full-width shot for 1.5s. Slide two thin cream dividers into place over 0.5s to reveal a deliberate 25% / 50% / 25% triptych: left is an environment or gesture detail, center is the hero action, right is a face or mechanical detail. Use different source moments or crops, never three identical copies; align the most important actions to meet at 5s. At 6s smoothly transfer the center panel's dominance to the right by resizing the panels over 12 frames, maintaining every subject's framing. At 9s make a clean synchronized match cut across all three panels. From 10.5–12s expand the strongest panel to full screen and finish on a satisfying moving frame. White balance all panels coherently and use warm off-white 5px gutters, no rounded app-card styling. Retain a continuous source ambience with gentle edit accents. No captions except small optional '01', '02', '03' outside faces. Deliver the MP4 and exact crop/timecode decisions. Every panel must visibly contribute a different view.

title: Cinematic Grade
description: A moving comparison reveals cool shadows and controlled warm highlights.
prompt: Create a 10-second cinematic color transformation from the same supplied Tears of Steel source. Select one continuous shot with a face, strong practical lights or glowing machinery, and meaningful shadow detail. For the first 1.25s show the untouched source. Then let a thin vertical comparison edge travel from left to right over 1.25s, revealing a carefully balanced nocturnal grade: deep cool shadows, warm controlled highlights, natural skin, gentle highlight rolloff, and readable blacks. During 2.5–7.5s give the graded image a very restrained 4% camera push while keeping the shot continuous and preserving its actual action. In the final 2.5s show a concise moving 50/50 original-versus-grade comparison with small crisp 'SOURCE' and 'AFTER DARK' labels in the lower safe area. The change must be obvious but tasteful—no crushed eyes, orange faces, excessive saturation, faux scratches, or synthetic grain. Do not call an already graded source LOG and do not add fake camera metadata. Preserve source ambience and use no new music. Deliver one 1920x1080 H264 MP4 plus source timecode and a concise list of the actual grading adjustments.

Original Canvas illustration, wordless, native 1920×1080, 30 fps, 10 seconds, deterministic absolute-time motion. No external assets.

title: Moon Laundromat
description: A mint washing machine tumbles socks, a small planet and a crescent moon in a lilac room. The round door swings open and a fresh crescent floats out into an arched window of midnight sky.
prompt: Authored prompt: A mint washing machine tumbles socks, a small planet and a crescent moon in a lilac room. The round door swings open and a fresh crescent floats out into an arched window of midnight sky. Original Canvas illustration, wordless, native 1920×1080, 30 fps, 10 seconds, deterministic absolute-time motion. No external assets.

title: Kinetic Typography
description: Letterforms negotiate space and open into a balanced moving poster.
prompt: Create a 12–16 second kinetic typography film about the words MAKE ROOM. Make the letterforms themselves compress, negotiate space, and open into a surprising beautifully balanced composition. Invent the choreography and typography. It should feel like an excellent moving graphic-design poster, with a strong visual payoff, not a succession of title cards.

title: Broadcast Identity
description: Acid-yellow typography and purple graphic shapes announce a night shift.
prompt: Create a 14–18 second broadcast identity for a fictional late-night culture channel called NIGHT SHIFT. Build an original flat graphic identity using framing, cropping, colour blocks and bold typography. Develop one recognisable graphic motif through several purposeful edits and a memorable end identity. No 3D objects, channel bugs copied from real broadcasters, or generic logo reveal.

title: Paper Collage
description: A paper river connects a map, photographic skyline, and open water.
prompt: Create a 15–20 second wordless editorial collage film about a river finding its way through a city. Use a coherent family of flat paper, print, map and photographic fragments, with tactile edges and surprising scale changes. A continuous visual connection should carry us through three distinct compositions. Invent or source your own permitted assets and keep it a designed collage, not slides with camera pans.

title: Character Animation
description: A small cloud helps a seed grow into a flower.
prompt: Create a charming 12–16 second flat illustrated micro-story: a small cloud tries to water one stubborn seed, and the seed gives the cloud an unexpected gift. Draw an original simple character language with expressive poses, clear cause and effect and a satisfying ending. Make the motion feel hand-authored and playful. No explanatory text, 3D, or stock cartoon assets.

title: Geometric Weaving
description: Colorful strands cross and transform into woven graphic patterns.
prompt: Create a 10–14 second optical graphic-design loop in which coloured lines exchange foreground and background, become an interlaced fabric, and resolve into the starting state. Make a distinctive composition with intentional visual rhythm and a few surprising changes in scale. Flat geometry, beautiful colour relationships, no words, no particles, and no 3D product study. The loop should actually join cleanly.

title: Animated Lettering
description: Ink gestures connect and resolve into expressive lettering.
prompt: Create a 12–18 second original lettering animation centred on the word again. A moving ink stroke should pass energy between the letters, with convincing drawn stroke construction and an inventive transformation through the word counterforms. Choose a distinctive lettering style and restrained paper/ink palette. The word must read clearly at the payoff; avoid typing-on text or cycling fonts.

title: Interface Animation
description: A planner interface turns scattered tasks into one good day.
prompt: Create a 15–20 second product UI motion story for a fictional day planner called One Good Day. Show a crowded day becoming manageable through one beautifully legible interaction that reorganises tasks into a calm timeline. Design the interface from scratch with excellent typography, continuity and hierarchy. Use close framing and purposeful transitions, no rotating devices, floating 3D screens, feature-list slides or implementation labels.

title: Geometric Choreography
description: Three simple shapes trade weight, rhythm, and balance.
prompt: Create a 10–15 second silent visual jazz performance using a small original family of flat graphic shapes. Give each shape its own rhythmic personality; let them trade a motif, interrupt, improvise and end together. Invent the composition and colour system. It must communicate rhythm through actual choreography and staging without music, text, equaliser bars, particles or 3D objects.

title: Object Assembly
description: A glossy red telephone forms around its curling cord.
prompt: Make a glossy red rotary telephone spring into shape as its coiled cord draws a looping path.

title: Glass Cascade
description: Colored glass tiles cascade into a sculptural spiral.
prompt: Make a stack of translucent colored glass tiles cascade into a spiral staircase.

title: Radial Reveal
description: Peppermint stripes bloom into a sun umbrella.
prompt: Make a striped beach umbrella bloom from a spinning peppermint disc.

title: Fluid Morph
description: A blue ink droplet grows eight curling arms and swims.
prompt: Make a single blue ink droplet become a swimming octopus.

title: Fabric Reveal
description: A silver zipper opens midnight fabric onto a river of color.
prompt: Make a silver zipper unzip a midnight surface and reveal a flowing river of color.

title: Origami
description: A red paper square unfolds into a swimming koi.
prompt: Make a red paper koi unfold from a square and swim through blue ink ripples.

title: Squash and Stretch
description: A soft cherry-red chair lands, squashes, and recovers.
prompt: Make a cherry-red jelly chair land, squash, and spring back into shape.

title: Mechanical Unfolding
description: A metallic beetle opens its wing cases and takes flight.
prompt: Make a chrome beetle open its wing cases and take flight.

title: Liquid Typography
description: Yellow letters liquefy and draw themselves back together.
prompt: Make the word MELT turn into warm yellow liquid and pull itself back into letters.

title: Ribbon Motion
description: A continuous fuchsia ribbon gathers into a floating bow.
prompt: Make a satin ribbon tie itself into a floating bow.

title: Exploded View
description: Ruby orange slices spiral open and snap back into one fruit.
prompt: Make a blood orange split into juicy slices, spiral open, and snap back together.

title: Miniature Animation
description: A tiny locomotive pulls a ceramic landscape into place.
prompt: Make a tiny train race around a ceramic planet and pull its landscape into place.

title: Organic Motion
description: A translucent bell pulses above trailing luminous ribbons.
prompt: Make a translucent jellyfish pulse through an inky sea, trailing glowing ribbons.

title: Pattern Morph
description: Checker cells become stripes as a running zebra takes shape.
prompt: Make a checkerboard peel itself into a galloping zebra.

title: Metal Morph
description: A chrome filament opens, threads through itself, and transforms.
prompt: Create a 16-second wordless motion film with a single chrome filament as the hero. Choreograph it from an open strand into a loop, through a threading transformation, and into a satisfying final form. Use polished reflections, dark studio lighting, deliberate camera movement, and no sound. No titles or supporting copy.

title: Bubble Optics
description: Macro bubble imagery connects to a clear thin-film interference diagram.
prompt: Make a short, beautiful explanation of why soap bubbles have rainbow colors.

title: Jet Engines
description: Real engine footage leads into a persistent animated cross-section.
prompt: Explain how a jet engine works using real footage and a continuous cutaway diagram. Show intake, compression, combustion, turbine work, and the faster exhaust that produces thrust.

title: GPU Dataflow
description: Follow data through GPU memory, parallel arithmetic, and result writeback.
prompt: Create a silent visual explanation of data moving through a GPU. Follow inputs from global memory through shared cache and parallel arithmetic, then return the computed results to memory.

title: Diffusion Models
description: A small image becomes noise, then a learned denoising process builds a new sample.
prompt: Create a beginner-friendly explainer about diffusion models. Show how adding noise creates training examples, how a network learns a correction, and how repeated denoising generates an image from fresh noise.

title: Binary Search
description: A sorted array makes each comparison and discarded half visible.
prompt: Make a concise narrated explainer of binary search. Show a target being found by repeatedly halving a sorted array, then connect the demonstration to searching one million items in at most twenty comparisons.

title: Hash Collisions
description: Follow two keys into one bucket and compare them along a linked chain.
prompt: Explain how a hash map handles collisions with separate chaining. Keep the bucket array visible as two keys land at one index, preserve both entries, then demonstrate a lookup comparing full keys until it finds the right value.

title: Split Screen
description: A complete podcast exchange with synchronized stacked speakers and clean captions.
prompt: Turn one compelling podcast exchange into a polished 25–40 second vertical clip. Find a source episode with two visible speakers and a complete surprising or useful thought. Stack the guest above the host using distinct, synchronized crops from the same conversation, separated by a thin white line. Add clean white phrase captions near the divider without covering faces. Remove dead air, preserve the speaker’s meaning and natural reactions, and end on the payoff. No unrelated background footage.

title: Auto Captions
description: A 44-second Jensen Huang interview highlight with vertical framing and burned captions.
prompt: Turn this interview recording into one postable vertical clip, 30 to 60 seconds, with burned captions. Pick the strongest self-contained moment yourself. Preserve the speaker’s meaning, remove dead space, keep the subject comfortably framed, and make the captions easy to read on a phone.

title: Metal Folding
description: A sculptural copper surface pleats, curls, and unfolds.
prompt: Create a 16-second wordless motion film starring one copper folding sculpture. Animate the material through precise pleats, a curl, and a full unfolding. Keep the sculpture centered, with warm directional light that reveals the metallic surface and a restrained camera move. Keep it silent. No titles or supporting copy.

title: Reaction Cuts
description: Conan tries to get a straight answer from Jordan Schlansky.
prompt: Make a 30–50 second comedy cut from one original Conan and Jordan Schlansky segment. Find a self-contained absurd exchange with a clear setup, escalation, punchline, and reaction. Reframe deliberately for vertical, keep both people visible when the reaction matters, and caption their actual words in clean white text. Tighten pauses that drag but protect comic hesitation and the final reaction. No canned laughter, fabricated dialogue, or distracting meme effects.

title: Step Selection
description: A cooking tutorial becomes a concise recipe with intact technique and clear timing.
prompt: Turn one original cooking tutorial into a useful 25–40 second vertical recipe short. Choose a visually satisfying dish with a few clear steps. Open on the finished result, then show ingredients, decisive technique, transformation, and a final serving shot. Cut on hand actions, retain crisp kitchen sounds, and use minimal readable ingredient and step labels grounded in the recipe. Preserve essential quantities and timings; compress waiting time without making the instructions misleading.

title: Restoration Montage
description: A corroded hand drill is dismantled, repaired, reassembled, and tested.
prompt: Create a 25–40 second satisfying restoration short from one original long-form workshop video. Establish the damaged object, then show a coherent progression through dismantling, cleaning, repair, reassembly, and a working reveal. Match actions across cuts, vary wide and detail views, and let real tool sounds drive the rhythm. Use a restrained before/after comparison and only essential labels. Keep the causal steps honest; the final object must be the same one shown at the beginning.

title: Travel Montage
description: A travel vlog becomes a short journey through arrival, discoveries, and rain.
prompt: Edit one original travel vlog into a 25–40 second vertical micro-story of a day in one place. Move from arrival through two or three distinct discoveries to a satisfying evening or departure. Use purposeful match cuts, a few natural-sound moments, and an independently sourced music bed that supports the changes in energy. Reframe people and landmarks carefully, avoid repeated scenic shots, and use only a few accurate location labels. Make it feel like a lived experience rather than a slideshow.

title: Shape Morph
description: Blue sparks become capsules, ribbons, rings, and a pinwheel.
prompt: Create a 15-second wordless motion film with luminous blue shapes. Develop one continuous transformation from sparks to capsules, then ribbons, a ring, and a pinwheel. Give each state a clear readable moment and make each transition flow naturally into the next. Use a dark studio background and no sound. No UI, labels, or supporting text.

title: Sports Montage
description: A music-led sequence of Messi goals builds into celebration.
prompt: Create a roughly 60-second Lionel Messi goals montage to Joy Crookes’ Feet Don’t Fail Me Now. Source sharp footage with yt-dlp, preferably one official goals compilation. Build from anticipation into increasingly spectacular goals and a joyful celebration. Preserve enough buildup and ball travel to understand every goal; land selected finishes on musical accents. Keep the song continuous, use crowd sound sparingly, and avoid repetitive replays, intrusive text, or effects hiding the football. Deliver widescreen 1080p.

title: Film Montage
description: Homemade heroics, wrestling spectacle, and a comic baptism payoff.
prompt: Make a 45–60 second Nacho Libre reel to Mister Loco’s original Religious Man. Begin with Nacho’s wonderfully serious face and homemade costume, keep the stretchy-pants joke and its reaction, then build through increasingly spectacular wrestling to the science line and sudden baptism gag. Source original scenes with yt-dlp. Keep music continuous, dialogue intact, and action readable. Use a centered full-width widescreen strip on a black portrait canvas, with compact white in-picture captions and selective red emphasis only during dialogue. No generic effects or title intro.

title: Food Review
description: A long food vlog becomes one focused story of preparation, first bite, and verdict.
prompt: Cut a long food-review vlog into a cohesive 50–75 second vertical story about one standout dish. Start with an irresistible real reaction, establish what and where it is, show preparation and texture, then let the first bite and honest verdict pay off. Use one original creator upload, such as Mark Wiens or Best Ever Food Review Show. Weave its own food close-ups under intact speech, remove repetition, add accurate clean captions, and preserve appetizing color and cooking sounds.

title: Mechanical Assembly
description: An eight-blade optical mechanism pulls apart and closes into place.
prompt: Create an eight-second, wordless 3D study of an optical aperture. Assemble eight metallic blades, open and close the iris, then separate the parts in a controlled exploded view. Use brushed metal, soft studio lighting, a dark background, and a slow deliberate camera. Keep every transformation mechanically clear.
